newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds finish nearly flat after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds finish nearly flat after quiet day.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed almost steady in lackluster trading on Thursday as investors paused after recent market volatility.
"Reasonably light activity, but a slight positive bias," said Mark Chandler, senior economist at Goldman Sachs Canada.
Chandler added that the long end of the curve looked firmer, but market players were concerned about the short-term bonds, which were weighed down by a weak Canadian dollar.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.03 to C$119.15 to yield 6.464 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.43 percent and the spread between the bonds remained unchanged at three basis points from Wednesday's close.
North American market players took a break after Tuesday's rally on positive comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and Wednesday's consolidation.
But the short end suffered from investor concerns as Canada's currency remained soft, Chandler said.
Some selling interests seemed intent on forcing the Bank of Canada to hike short-term interest rates for a second time this year, another analyst said.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dipped C$0.02 to reach C$109.80 to yield 5.920 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond slipped 1/32 to yield 6.16 percent, so the negative spread between the bonds stayed steady at 24 basis points from Wednesday's close.
